messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired for `synth-canary-us-west` — 6 consecutive probe failures (consec_fail_threshold=5). Probe ID: canary-usw-17. See run: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/PROBER/canary-usw

pagerduty: Incident triggered: PD-INC-88921 -> paging @oncall-sre (primary). Link: https://pd.redwood.ai/incidents/PD-INC-88921

Raj P: acked via PD. I'm on it. Can someone confirm user-facing impact?

Marta R: looking at grafana, prod 5xx pct steady at ~0.2%, no broad user spikes. This is isolated to the synthetic probe cluster in us-west. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/prober/canaries

Sam (sre): ran a quick curl vs the probe target: `curl -i https://canary-usw.redwood.ai/health` -> `HTTP/2 503` with body "service temporarily unavailable". Reproduces from our jumpbox.

Azadeh K: thanks. Could be a routing flap or a backend pool mis-tag. Can we disable the noisy probe temporarily to stop paging while we triage?

Raj P: doing that now. Command: ```
./infra/proberctl disable --probe canary-usw-17 --reason "noisy synthetic failures" --ttl 10m
```

incident-bot: Action logged: prober disabled by Raj P (ttl=10m). PagerDuty note updated.

Marta R: after disabling probe I still see sporadic 5xx from that pool in edge logs (sample): `edge-reqid=ab12cd status=503 backend=lb-usw-3 latency=142ms`. Small volume — likely a backend pool issue.

Sam (sre): I can tail the backend service (genie-inference-usw). Attaching logs snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T12:03:21Z] ERROR http: worker id=23 request=0x7fae status=503 err="kv cache miss->timeout"
[2026-03-15T12:03:22Z] ERROR http: worker id=17 request=0x7fad status=503 err="upstream read timeout"
```

Raj P: thanks. If backend is flapping, we should failover traffic away from the affected pool. Ops runbook step: `trafficctl set-weight lb-usw-3 0.0 --dry-run=false` — do we want to do that?

Azadeh K: agreed. I'll coordinate with infra to drain that pool and trigger autoscaler if needed. Doing `trafficctl drain lb-usw-3` now.

Customer Success Bot: FYI — no customer tickets opened yet. Monitoring CS mentions for the next 30m.

Marta R: draining appears to reduce error rate on edge within 30s. Canaries produce green on rerun from eu-west copy.

Sam (sre): reran the health check post-drain: `HTTP/2 200 OK` from the canary endpoint. Looks like removing the bad node stabilized requests.

Raj P: updating PD incident with mitigation steps. PD note: "drained lb-usw-3, disabled noisy probe, verified health checks passing".

pagerduty: PD-INC-88921 updated, escalation halted. Current status: acknowledged -> monitoring.

Azadeh K: we'll keep the prober disabled for another 10m, then re-enable with a more conservative threshold (consec_fail_threshold=8) while we watch. Raj, can you create a follow-up ticket for postmortem if this recurs?

Raj P: created ticket INC-2026-331 in ops-tracker with root cause hypothesis: transient backend timeouts after deployment of kernel patch (kpatch-1.4.2) to lb-usw-3. Assigned to Sam.

Sam (sre): will own the follow-up. Quick note: suggest adding a runbook check to correlate prober failures with kpatch events.

Marta R: CS loop — no current customer impact detected, but we should proactively notify any customers with heavy usage in us-west if we see repeated flaps.

Raj P: ok handing off to Azadeh in 10m for next-oncall continuity. Azadeh, ping me if rollback is needed.

Azadeh K: acknowledged. I'll stay on for the handoff. Also scheduling an alert suppression window: `incident-bot suppress-alert synth-canary-us-west 15m --reason "mitigated, verifying"`

incident-bot: Alert suppression scheduled for `synth-canary-us-west` (15m). PD-INC-88921 set to status: resolved -> awaiting follow-up.

Sam (sre): final check — sample client logs show a tiny uptick in retry attempts from background jobs (~0.02% of requests) around the time of the flap. Noted in INC-2026-331.

Raj P: thanks team. If anything else pops, escalate to SRE-2. Otherwise I'll close the slack thread after handoff. :white_check_mark:
